rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God found Muhammad without possessions and enriched him through profitable trade with Maysara in Syria, Khadija's wealth after marriage, and Abu Bakr's wealth.
rows.anchor: وذلك في سفره صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم مع ميسرة إلى الشام وبما وهبته لك خديجة رضي الله تعالى عنها من المال

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some interpret enrichment as spoils, but al-Alusi objects that the surah is Meccan and spoils came only after the Hijra.
rows.anchor: وقيل بما أفاء عليك من الغنائم وفيه أن السورة مكية والغنائم إنما كانت بعد الهجرة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that God enriched him by contentment and a self-sufficient heart, since true wealth is inward contentment.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد قنعك وأغنى قلبك فإن غنى القلب هو الغنى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Enrichment can mean God made him independent of all besides Him; this is a wealth rooted in need of God, echoed by a supplication and a poem.
rows.anchor: وقيل أغناك به عز وجل عما سواه وهذا الغنى بالأفتقار إليه تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن حجر
rows.claim: Ibn Hajar calls the popular report Poverty is my pride fabricated and false.
rows.anchor: وحمل الفقر فيه على هذا المعنى وهو على ما قال ابن حجر باطل موضوع

rows.speaker: بعض المتصوفة
rows.claim: Al-Alusi condemns the Sufi saying that perfected poverty is God as false and repugnant.
rows.anchor: إذا تم الفقر فهو الله سبحانه وتعالى عما يقولون علوا كبيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root may mean having many dependents, but al-Alusi prefers the meaning of lacking property, supported by Ibn Masud's reading عديمًا and the Prophet's early circumstances.
rows.anchor: ورجح الأول في الآية بقراءة ابن مسعود عديما وأنه عليه الصلاة والسلام لم يكن ذا عيال في أول أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Yemenite reading عيلا with a doubled, kasra-marked yāʾ is also reported.
rows.anchor: وقرأ اليماني عيلا كسا بشد الياء المكسورة

rows.speaker: عصام الدين
rows.claim: Isam al-Din allegorizes the orphan as lacking a teacher, misguidance as lack of knowledge, and dependents as the religious community needing guidance; al-Alusi finds this unpersuasive.
rows.anchor: وذكر عصام الدين في هذه الآيات أنه يحتمل أن يراد باليتيم فاقد المعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objects of the three verbs are omitted because they are clear from context and to preserve the rhyme; an expansive alternative wording does not fit the verbs.
rows.anchor: وحدث المفعول في الأفعال الثلاثة لظهور المراد مع رعاية الفواصل

rows.speaker: ابن سلام
rows.claim: Ibn Salam explains the command as not humiliating the orphan.
rows.anchor: فلا تستذله كما قال ابن سلام

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says not to despise the orphan.
rows.anchor: وقريب منه قول مجاهد لا تحتقر

rows.speaker: سفيان
rows.claim: Sufyan explains it as not wronging the orphan by wasting his property; a related view forbids taking it over.
rows.anchor: وقال سفيان لا تظلمه بتضييع ماله وفي معناه ما قيل لا تغلبه على ماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi favors taking oppression as both overpowering and humiliating, or as a shared word carrying both senses.
rows.anchor: ولعل التقييد لمراعاة الغالب والأولى حمل القهر على الغلبة والتذليل معا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Masud, al-Shabi, and Ibrahim al-Taymi read تكهر with hāʾ; lexicons give overpowering, frowning, or cursing, and al-Alusi favors the middle sense, frowning.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود والشعبي وإبراهيم التيمي فلا تكهر بالحاف بدل القاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whichever lexical sense is chosen, the verse urges care for orphans; forbidding a frown also entails forbidding cursing and oppression a fortiori.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى فلا تعبس في وجهه وهو نهي عن الشتم والقهر على ما سمعت من معناه من باب الأولى

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: A report attributed to Ibn Masud from the Prophet promises a light on Judgment Day for each hair touched when an orphan's head is stroked; its transmission is criticized.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود مرفوعا من مسح على رأس يتيم كان له بكل شعرة تمر عليها يده نور يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: A report attributed to Umar says an orphan's crying shakes the Throne and that God will please the person who comforts the orphan; Umar reportedly stroked orphans' heads and gave them gifts.
rows.anchor: وعن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنه مرفوعا أيضا أن اليتيم إذا بكى اهتز لبكائه عرش الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No sound report establishes a particular manner for stroking an orphan's head, and the Ibn Masud narration has been questioned.
rows.anchor: ولم يصح في كيفية مسحه شيء والرواية عن ابن مسعود في ذلك قد قيل فيها ما قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic report compares the caretaker of an orphan who fears God with the Prophet as two fingers held together.
rows.anchor: أنا وكافل اليتيم كهاتين إذا اتقى الله عز وجل وأشار بالسبابة والوسطى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The asker should not be rebuked and should instead be treated generously; many take the asker to mean someone seeking material aid.
rows.anchor: أي فلا تزجره ولكن تفضل عليه بشيء أورده بقول جميل وأريد به عند جمع السائل المستجدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse likewise signals care for the person who asks.
rows.anchor: وتدل الآية على الأعتناء بشأنه أيضا

rows.speaker: إبراهيم بن أدهم
rows.claim: Ibrahim ibn Adham praises beggars for carrying people's provisions to the afterlife through the opportunity to give.
rows.anchor: وعن إبراهيم ابن أدهم نعم القول السؤال يحملون زادنا إلى الآخرة

rows.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
rows.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakhai says a seeker of the afterlife comes to one's door asking whether one will send something to one's family.
rows.anchor: وعن إبراهيم النخعي السائل يريد الآخرة يجيء إلى باب أحدكم

rows.speaker: الإمام أحمد
rows.claim: Ahmad says the report that an asker has a right even when arriving on horseback has no basis; Abu Dawud transmits it from al-Husayn as a stopped report, while al-Iraqi calls its chain good and Ibn Abd al-Barr calls it weak.
rows.anchor: وقد قال فيه الإمام أحمد كما في تمييز الطيب من الخبيث لا أصل له

rows.speaker: ابن المديني
rows.claim: The report that no one who turns away an honest asker prospers has no basis according to Ibn al-Madini; Ibn Abd al-Barr says all its chains are weak, while al-Tabarani has a similar Prophetic report from Abu Umama that al-Alusi has not seen criticized.
rows.anchor: روي من طرق عن عائشة وغيرها لو صدق السائل ما أفلح من رده وهو أيضا على ما قال ابن المديني لا أصل له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ban on rebuking applies when the asker is not persistent; if persistence continues and gentle refusal fails, rebuking is allowed.
rows.anchor: ثم النهي على النهر على ما قالوا إذا لم يلح في السؤال فإن ألح ولم ينفع الرد اللين فلا بأس بالزجر

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء، الحسن، سفيان
rows.claim: Abu al-Darda, Hasan, Sufyan, and others interpret the asker as a student asking about knowledge and religion, not a petitioner for money.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الدرداء والحسن وسفيان وغيرهم المراد بالسائل هنا السائل عن العلم والدين لا سائل المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi leans toward the knowledge-seeker interpretation: neglecting a capable person's question about knowledge brings a threat, unlike not giving alms to a petitioner one can afford to refuse.
rows.anchor: ويشهد للأولوية أنه أنه لا وعيد على ترك أعطاء المستجدي لمن يجد ما يستجديه بخلاف ترك جواب سائل العلم لمن يعلم

rows.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز، الحسن، قتادة، الفضيل بن عياض
rows.claim: These authorities say that speaking of God's bounty is an expression of gratitude for it.
rows.anchor: فإن التحدث بها شكر لها كما قال عمر بن عبد العزيز والحسن وقتادة والفضيل بن عياض

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says one who receives a gift should reciprocate, or praise the giver if unable; praise counts as gratitude and concealment as ingratitude. Al-Alusi gives no grading.
rows.anchor: من أعطى فوجد فليجز به فإن لم يجد فليثن به فمن أثنى به فقد شكره

rows.speaker: بعض السلف
rows.claim: Some early Muslims recommend recounting one's good deeds when the aim is example rather than showing off or boasting.
rows.anchor: استحب بعض السلف التحدث بما عمله من الخير إذا لم يرد به الرياء والأفتخار وعلم الأقتداء به

rows.speaker: الحسن بن علي
rows.claim: Hasan ibn Ali interprets the command as a believer telling his household about a righteous deed; elsewhere he says to share good fortune with one's brothers.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن مقسم قال لقيت الحسن بن علي بن أبي طالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bounty most likely means the many kinds of blessing God bestowed on the Prophet, including the blessings just mentioned.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بالنعمة ما أفاضه الله تعالى على نبيه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم من فنون النعم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets the bounty as prophethood in one report and the Quran in another; Ibn Ishaq agrees on prophethood, while al-Kalbi and Ali ibn Abi Talib agree on the Quran, with proclaiming as the sense of speaking.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر وغيره عن مجاهد تفسيرها بالنبوة ورووا عنه أيضا تفسيرها بالقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi finds both the prophethood and Quran interpretations ill-suited to the preceding context.
rows.anchor: ولا يخفى أن كلا التفسيرين غير مناسب لما قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three commands form a reordered correspondence with the preceding orphanhood, lost guidance, and poverty: remember those gifts and show compassion to orphans and seekers as one who experienced orphanhood and need.
rows.anchor: وحاصل المعنى أنك كنت يتيما وضالا وعائلا فآواك وهداك وإناك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence is explained as putting human rights before God's right, or as cleansing before adornment, rhetorical progression, or rhyme; al-Alusi scrutinizes these explanations.
rows.anchor: ولم يراع الترتيب لتقديم حقوق العباد على حقه عز وجل فإنه سبحانه وتعالى غني عن العالمين

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Tibi says that if the asker is a knowledge-seeker the sequence follows the order of the Prophet's own circumstances: early discernment and guidance, then enrichment after the mission, with each command corresponding to a divine gift.
rows.anchor: وقال الطيبي الظاهر أن المراد بالسائل طالب العلم لا المستجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording فحدث is preferred over فأخبر so the Prophet's mention of blessing becomes a recurring remembrance.
rows.anchor: وآثر سبحانه فحدث على فخبر قيل ليكون ذكر النعمة منه عليه الصلاة والسلام حديثا لا ينساه

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: A report traces the practice of making takbir at the end of this and later surahs to the Prophet through Ibn Abbas, Ubayy ibn Kab, Mujahid, Ibn Kathir, and others; it presents takbir as joy at revelation resuming after delay, and al-Alusi says people follow this practice.
rows.anchor: وأخبره عبد الله ابن كثير أنه قرأ على مجاهد فأمره بذلك وأخبره أن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أمره بذلك

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير، عائشة
rows.claim: The surah is called al-Sharh and is reported Meccan by Ibn al-Zubayr and Aisha; Ibn Abbas is also reported to say it followed al-Duha.
rows.anchor: وتسمى سورة الشرح وهي كما روي عن ابن الزبير وعائشة مكية

rows.speaker: البقاعي
rows.claim: Al-Biqai argues that it is Medinan from a report that the verse about ease with hardship was revealed in Medina; al-Alusi doubts the report's soundness.
rows.anchor: وزعم البقاعي أنها عنده مدنية حديث طويل أخرجه ابن مردويه عن جابر بن عبد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah has eight verses by agreement and is very closely connected in meaning to al-Duha.
rows.anchor: وآيها ثمان بالإتفاق وهي شديدة الإتصال بسورة الضحى

rows.speaker: طاوس، عمر بن عبد العزيز
rows.claim: Tawus and Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz treated al-Duha and al-Sharh as one surah, reciting them together without the basmala between them; Shia practice is also reported this way.
rows.anchor: حتى أنه روي عن طاوس وعمر بن عبد العزيز أنهما كانا يقولان هما سورة واحدة

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: One objection to treating them as one surah is that al-Duha describes distress while the chest-expansion wording implies ease, so their revelation states would not fit together.
rows.anchor: لأن الأول كان عند اغتنام الرسول صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم من إيذاءه الكفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi answers that transmitted reports govern this question, and the established transmission is that they are two surahs separated by the basmala, though closely linked in meaning.
rows.anchor: والحق أن مدار مثل ذلك الرواية لا الدارية والمتواتر كونهما سورتين والفصل بينهما بالبسملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report about the Night Journey has God remind Muhammad that He sheltered, guided, enriched him, expanded his chest, removed his burden, and raised his mention, demonstrating the surahs' thematic connection.
rows.anchor: يا محمد ألم أجدك يتيما فآويت وضالا فهديت وعائلا فأغنيت وشرحت لك صدرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: شرح originally means expansion and is also used for clarification; with the heart or chest it can mean gladness and expansion of the inner self, through a chain of place-based associations.
rows.anchor: الشرح في الأصل الفسح والتوسعة وشاع استعماله في الإيضاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other possible senses include increasing knowledge or strengthening the soul with sacred power and divine lights so it can receive and communicate knowledge without distraction.
rows.anchor: وقد يراد به إذا تعلق بالقلب أو الصدر أيضا تكثير ما فيه من المعلومات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For this context of divine favor, al-Alusi finds the strengthening of the prophetic soul most fitting: it encompasses unseen and visible realms and joins receiving knowledge to conveying it.
rows.anchor: والأنسب بمقام الأمتنان هنا إرادة هذا المعنى الأخير

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that God relieved the Prophet's anxiety by showing him realities and the world's insignificance, making hardship in calling people to God easier to bear.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى ألم نزل همك وغمك بإطلاعك على حقائق الأمور وحقارة الدنيا

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority explain the verse as expansion through wisdom and God's making it easier for the Prophet to receive revelation after it had initially been difficult.
rows.anchor: ونقل عن الجمهور أن المعنى ألم نفسحه بالحكمة وتوسعه بتيسيرنا لك تلقي ما يوحى إليك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وجماعة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and a group interpret the verse as a reference to the physical splitting of Muhammad's chest during childhood, supported by reports including one from his nurse Halima.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس وجماعة أنه إشارة إلى شق صدره الشريف في صباه عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: حليمة
rows.claim: Halima recounts that after Muhammad returned to her care as a toddler, his nursing brother saw two white-clad men lay him down, split his belly, remove something, and restore him; his parents returned him to his mother, who said the devil had no hold on him and that his destiny was great.
rows.anchor: فاضجعاه وشقا بطنه فخرجت أنا وأبوه نشتد نحوه فوجدناه قائما منتقعا لونه

rows.speaker: أبو يعلى، أبو نعيم، ابن عساكر
rows.claim: Reports in Abu Yala, Abu Nuaym, and Ibn Asakir indicate the chest-opening happened repeatedly while Muhammad was with Halima.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث لأبي يعلى وأبي نعيم وابن عساكر ما يدل على تكرر وقوع ذلك له عليه الصلاة والسلام وهو عند حليمة

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: A report transmitted in Musnad Ahmad's additions says Muhammad described an encounter in his twenties: two men split his chest without blood or pain, removed a clot-like object, placed something like silver representing compassion and mercy, and marked his right big toe; another wording places him at age ten.
rows.anchor: أن أبا هريرة قال يا رسول الله ما رأيت من أمر النبوة فاستوى رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم جالسا

rows.speaker: ابن حجر المكي
rows.claim: Ibn Hajar al-Makki gives another wording of the chest-splitting report that places the Prophet at ten years old, so the event could also have occurred before puberty.
rows.anchor: وفيه أني لفي صحراء واسعة ابن عشر حجج إذا أنا برجلين فوق رأسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These reports do not rule out an earlier chest-splitting incident, since the one associated with the onset of prophethood could be the later event.
rows.anchor: ليس نصا على نفي وقوع شق قبله لجواز أن يكون الذي استشعر منه النبوة هو هذا لا ما قبله

rows.speaker: الطيالسي، الحارث، أبو نعيم
rows.claim: Reports in the Musnads of al-Tayalisi and al-Harith and in Abu Nuaym say Gabriel and Michael split Muhammad's chest and washed it before Gabriel told him to read the opening revelation.
rows.anchor: قال اقرأ باسم ربك الآيات

rows.speaker: مالك بن صعصعة
rows.claim: A report narrated by the Prophet through Malik ibn Sasa and Anas describes the Night Journey: his chest was opened to the lower belly, his heart washed with Zamzam, then refilled with faith and wisdom before he rode al-Buraq.
rows.anchor: فشرح صدري إلى كذا وكذا قال قتادة قلت يعني لأنس ما تعني قال إلى أسفل بطني

rows.speaker: القاضي عبد الجبار
rows.claim: Qadi Abd al-Jabbar objects that a chest opening before prophethood would put a miracle before the mission, and after prophethood the washing and insertion of faith or wisdom make no sense spiritually.
rows.anchor: وطعن القاضي عيد الجبار في ذلك بما حاصله أنه يلزم على وقوعه في الصغر وقبل النبوة تقدم المعجزة على النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi replies that pre-prophetic miracles are valid as irhas, and physical washing may aid spiritual refinement by altering temperament; inserted compassion and faith can name their causes metaphorically or exist materially.
rows.anchor: فإن تقدم الخارق على النبوة جائز عندنا ونسميه إرهاصا والأخبار كثيرة في وقوعه له عليه الصلاة والسلام قبل النبوة

rows.speaker: ابن أبي جمرة
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Jamra argues that what prophetic speech presents as created substances beyond ordinary perception is materially real, so faith and wisdom may be sensible entities rather than abstractions.
rows.anchor: ما دل كلام النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم على جوهريته وجسميته من أعيان المخلوقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A possible alternative treats the chest opening and extracted heart as sensory representations that disclose spiritual realities; some scholars instead insist that the reported event must be believed literally and not interpreted away.
rows.anchor: لعل ذلك من باب التمثيل إذ تمثيل المعاني قد وقع كثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says the physical chest-splitting is a weak interpretation of this verse among critical scholars, despite the reports themselves being affirmed by many.
rows.anchor: نعم حمل الشرح في الآية على ذلك الشق ضعيف عند المحققين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question emphatically affirms expansion; the majestic plural marks its greatness, and fronting لك signals its benefit to the Prophet and hastens his gladness in anticipation of what follows.
rows.anchor: والتعبير عن ثبوت الشرح بالأستفهام الإنكاري عن انتفائه للإيذان بأن ثبوته من الظهور

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر المنصور
rows.claim: Abu Jafar al-Mansur is reported to read نشرح with an open final hāʾ; al-Alusi begins to discuss grammatical explanations in the following segment.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر المنصور ألم نشرح بفتح الحاء

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says deleting the emphatic ending is especially weak in this negative clause, even compared with the poetic example.
rows.anchor: ولا يخفى أن الحذف هنا أضعف مما في البيت

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni reports from Abu Mujahid that this emphatic-nun derivation is not permissible; the example verse cited for deletion may itself be fabricated.
rows.anchor: ولهذا روي ابن جني في المنتفي عن أبي مجاهد أنه غير جائز أصلا

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Al-Alusi prefers Abu Zayd's poetic example for dropping the emphatic ending over the allegedly fabricated horse verse.
rows.anchor: والأولى في التمثيل ما أنشده أبو زيد في نوادره

rows.speaker: الليحاني
rows.claim: Al-Bahr offers a better explanation: some Arabs use accusative with lam and jussive with lan, the reverse of common usage, supported by al-Lihyani's report and a line of poetry.
rows.anchor: وفي البحر أن لهذه القراءة تخريجا أحسن مما ذكر وهو أن الفتح على لغة بعض العرب من النصب بلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposal treats the open ending as attraction from what follows, analogous to reading الحمد لله with a genitive ending, though this cannot explain all the cited examples.
rows.anchor: وخرجها بعضهم على أن الفتح لمحاورة ما بعدها كالكسر في قراءة الحمد لله بالجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause coordinates with the implied sense of the previous one: God expanded the Prophet's chest and removed his burden.
rows.anchor: عطف على ما أشير إليه من مدلول الجملة السابقة كأنه قيل قد شرحنا لك صدرك ووضعنا الخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عنْك is fronted before the direct object to hasten the joyful news and suspense; leaving the long object before it would disrupt the verse's balanced phrasing.
rows.anchor: وتقديمه على المفعول الصريح لما مر من القصد إلى تعجيل المسرة والتشويق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وزر means a heavy load, so the phrase says God lifted the Prophet's heavy burden.
rows.anchor: والوزر الحمل الثقيل أي وحططنا عنك حملك الثقيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أنقض means to make a creaking or cracking sound as joints loosen; it also applies to joints, not only loads or people, and the line of Abbas ibn Mirdas depicts a burden making his back groan.
rows.anchor: الذي انقض ظهرك أي حمله على النقيض وهو صوت الأنتقاض والأنفكاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing the creaking to the load is a figurative attribution to its causing agent; the burden can mean pre-mission acts the Prophet found painful to recall, with its removal meaning forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وإسناد الإنقاض للحمل إسناد للسبب الحامل مجازا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other proposed burdens are the Prophet's lack of revealed knowledge of religious law, uncertainty about the message or its reception, and the difficulty of receiving revelation at first; removal means teaching or easing these matters.
rows.anchor: أو غفلته عن الشرائع ونحوها مما لا يدرك إلا بالوحي مع تطلبه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations are grief at his people's misguidance while unable to guide them, their abuse of him, or anxiety over Abu Talib's death and Khadija's death if the surah followed theirs; relief comes through converts such as Hamza and Umar or strengthened endurance.
rows.anchor: أو ما كان يرى صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم من ضلال قومه مع العجز عن إرشادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The removal is also interpreted as lifting the Prophet to heaven, where he met every angel and attained the vision of his beloved Lord.
rows.anchor: وعلى السابع إزالة ذلك برفعه إلى السماء حتى لقيه كل ملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whatever the intended burden, the expression is a representative metaphor, and the verse does not prove the Prophet was previously without protection from sin.
rows.anchor: وأيا ما كان ففي الكلام استعارة تمثيلية والوضع ترشيح لها وليس فيه دليل لنا في العصمة

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan takes the burden as sins and the removal as the Prophet's protection from sin and purification, phrased as a rhetorical exaggeration.
rows.anchor: واختار أبو حيان كون وضع الوزر كناية عن عصمته

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view makes the burden the sins of Muhammad's community, attributed to him because of his concern for them; its removal means preventing their immediate punishment while he is among them or they seek forgiveness, as in 8:33. Al-Alusi calls this remote.
rows.anchor: والتمثيل عليه بحاله على ما قيل المراد وزر أمتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anas reads حططنا or حللنا instead of وضعنا, while Ibn Masud reads عنك وقرك.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أنس وحططنا وحللنا مكان وضعنا وقرأ ابن مسعود عنك وقرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God raised Muhammad's mention through prophethood, pairing his name with God's in the testimony, pairing obedience with God's, blessing him and commanding believers to do so, addressing him by honored titles, mentioning him in earlier books, and taking covenants from earlier prophets and peoples to believe in him.
rows.anchor: بالنبوة وغيرها وأي رفع مثل أن قرن اسمه عليه الصلاة والسلام باسمه عز وجل في كلمتي الشهادة

rows.speaker: مجاهد، قتادة، محمد بن كعب، الضحاك، الحسن
rows.claim: These authorities explain the raised mention as meaning that whenever God is mentioned, Muhammad is mentioned with Him.
rows.anchor: روي عن مجاهد وقتادة ومحمد بن كعب والضحاك والحسن وغيرهم أنهم قالوا في ذلك لا أذكر إلا ذكرت معي

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: A Prophetic report from Abu Said says Gabriel told the Prophet that God raised his mention by ensuring that whenever He is mentioned, Muhammad is mentioned too.
rows.anchor: إن ربك يقول أتدري كيف رفعت ذكرك قلت الله تعالى أعلم

rows.speaker: حسان بن ثابت
rows.claim: Hassan ibn Thabit's poem celebrates the seal of prophethood and the joining of the Prophet's name to God's in the call to prayer as evidence of his honored mention.
rows.anchor: وضم الإله اسم النبي إلى اسمه إذا قال في الخمس المؤذن أشهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse may focus on the greatest instance of raised mention; placing it after the burden's removal and fronting لك continue the rhetorical pattern explained earlier.
rows.anchor: وكان ذلك من الأقتصار على ما هو أعظم قدرا من أفراد رفع الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When finished with an act of worship such as conveying revelation, the Prophet should exert himself in another act of worship, giving thanks for past favors and promised future gifts and leaving no time empty of worship.
rows.anchor: أي من عبادة كتبليغ الوحي فانصب فاتعب في عبادة أخرى شكرا لما عددنا عليك من النعم السالفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should direct his desire and supplication to his Lord alone, since only God can provide assistance.
rows.anchor: وإلى ربك وحده فارغب فاحرص بالسؤال ولا تسألأ غيره تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, and Qatada say that after prayer one should devote oneself to supplication.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير وغيره من طرق عن ابن عباس أنه قال أي إذا فرغت من الصلاة فانصب في الدعاء

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud says that after the obligatory prayers one should devote oneself to night vigil.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر عن ابن مسعود أي إذا فرغت من الفرائض فانصب في قيام الليل

rows.speaker: الحسن، زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Hasan and, similarly, Zayd ibn Aslam say that after a military campaign one should strive in worship; the objection that the surah is Meccan may be answered by positing a Medinan surah or verse, or a delayed ruling.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن أي إذا فرغت من الغزو فاجتهد في العبادة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says that after finishing one's worldly affairs one should pray; in another report his view resembles Ibn Abbas's.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن نصر وجماعة عن مجاهد أي إذا فرغت من أسباب نفسك وفي لفظ من دنياك فصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi prefers the general worship sense and treats the specific prayer, supplication, and night vigil interpretations as examples; prayer and supplication may be singled out as central forms of worship.
rows.anchor: والأنسب حمل الآية على ما تقدم وأما قول ابن عباس ومن معه فهو تخصيص لبعض العبادات

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid's worldly-work reading draws on the common use of فراغ for freedom from worldly business, as in the saying to seize free time before becoming occupied; al-Alusi calls it the weakest view because it poorly fits the context and fa.
rows.anchor: وقول مجاهد نظر فيه إلى أن الفراغ أكثر ما يستعمل في الخلو عن الأشغال الدنيوية

rows.speaker: عصام الدين
rows.claim: Isam al-Din interprets the sequence as moving from one hardship to another in pursuit of two eases; al-Alusi says this is far from the ordinary sense.
rows.anchor: وقال عصام الدين لا نسب أن يراد فإذا فرغت من يسر فانصب بعسر آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage recommends filling one's time with worship or turning to worship once worldly affairs are done; Umar disliked idleness, and Sharik rebuked men for wrestling instead of productive work.
rows.anchor: وأشعرت الآية بأن اللائق يحال العبد أن يستغرق أوقاته بالعبادة

rows.speaker: أبو السمال
rows.claim: Abu al-Sammal reads فرغت with a kasra on the rāʾ, a dialectal form that al-Zamakhshari calls inelegant.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال فرغت بكسر الراء وهي لغة قال الزمخشري ليست بفصيحة

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some read فأنصب with a doubled open yāʾ from the form meaning to exert oneself, interpreted as turning wholly to another act of worship.
rows.anchor: وقرأ قوم فأنصب بشد الياء مفتوحة من الإنصاب

rows.speaker: بعض الإمامية
rows.claim: Some Imamis allege a reading with kasra on the ṣād and interpret it as appointing Ali to the imamate after prophethood; al-Alusi says the verse does not specify the person, and Sunnis can supply Abu Bakr based on the prayer-leadership report and the timing before the Prophet's death.
rows.anchor: ونسب إلى بعض الإمامية أنه قرأ فأنصب بكسر الصاد فقيل أي فإذا فرغت من النبوة فانصب عليا للأمامة

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf says that if the Imami reading were valid, an anti-Ali reader could construe نصب as ordering hatred of Ali; al-Alusi finds this objection flawed.
rows.anchor: وقال في الكشاف لو صح ذلك للرافضي لصح للناصي أن يقرأ هكذا

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya calls the Imami reading anomalous and weak in meaning, not established from any recognized scholar.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية إن هذه القراءة شاذة ضعيفة المعنى لم تثبت عن عالم

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي، ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Ali and Ibn Abi Abla read فرغب as an imperative with doubled ghayn, meaning invite people to seek what God has.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي وابن أبي عبلة فرغب أمر من رغب بشد الغين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Surat al-Tin is also called al-Tin without the conjunction; most say it is Meccan, while Qatada and a report from Ibn Abbas call it Medinan. The reference to the secure city is unanimously taken as Mecca, supporting the majority; all agree on eight verses.
rows.anchor: ويقال لها سورة التين بلا واو مكية في قول الجمهور وعن قتادة أنها مدنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the preceding surah described Muhammad as the most perfect human, this surah discusses humanity's condition and end and God's reward for those who follow that exemplary figure.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر سبحانه في السورة السابقة حال أكمل النوع الإنساني بالإتفاق بل أكمل خلق الله

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority take the address as generic humanity, with a shift of person intensifying rebuke; fa derives the rebuke from the prior proof, and the ba marks cause. الدين means recompense after resurrection.
rows.anchor: عند الجمهور للإنسان على طريقة الألتفات لتشديد التوبيخ والتبكيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human creation and its astonishing proportions and transformations plainly prove God's power to resurrect and repay; after that proof, what can make a person deny recompense? Every denier of truth is a liar.
rows.anchor: إن خلق الإنسان من نطفة وتقويمه على وجه يبهر الأذهان ويضيق عنه نطاق البيان

rows.speaker: قتادة، الأخفش، الفراء
rows.claim: Qatada, al-Akhfash, and al-Farra say the Prophet is addressed: after the clear proof, what could make anyone call you a liar about recompense? The rhetorical challenge indirectly rebukes deniers and underscores the Prophet's unwavering certainty.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة والأخفش والفراء الخطاب للرسول صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the Prophet-address interpretation, ba may mean within the message or because of the message, with an implicit noun, or it may mark the object of denial and make الدين mean Islam; Mujahid and Qatada are cited for the latter.
rows.anchor: وجوز على هذا الوجه كون الباء بمعنى في وكونها السببية وتقدير مضاف عليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposal that ما means من makes the meaning clearer for some, but al-Alusi rejects it as an unfamiliar use when the ordinary meaning of ما works.
rows.anchor: وضعف بأنه خلاف المعروف في ما فلا ينبغي ارتكابه مع صحة بقائها على المعروف فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who created humanity must be the wisest in action and governance; denying resurrection would imply otherwise, so resurrection is necessary. The question confirms the preceding point.
rows.anchor: أي أليس الذي فعل ما ذكر بأحكم الحاكمين صنعا وتدبيرا حتى يتوهم عدم الإعادة والجزاء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes الحكم as judgment, making the verse a warning that God will judge the disbelievers according to what they deserve in punishment.
rows.anchor: وقيل الحكم بمعنى القضاء فهي وعيد للكفار وأنه عز وجل يحكم عليهم بما هم أهله

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says that a reader reaching this verse should answer, Yes indeed, and I am among those who bear witness; another report says the Prophet would say, Glory be to You, yes indeed.
rows.anchor: من قرأ منكم والتين والزيتون فانتهى إلى قوله تعالى أليس الله بأحكم الحاكمين فليقل بلى وأنا على ذلك من الشاهدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Surat Iqra is Meccan without dispute, but its verse count differs: twenty in the Hijazi count, nineteen Iraqi, and eighteen Syrian.
rows.anchor: وتسمى سورة اقرأ لا خلاف في مكيتها وإنما الخلاف في عدد آيها

rows.speaker: أبو رجاء العطاردي
rows.claim: Many say Iqra was the first revelation; Abu Musa's student Abu Raja reports that Abu Musa called it the first surah sent to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: أخرج الطبراني في الكبير بسنده على شرط الصحيح عن أبي رجاء العطاردي

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi authenticate a report from Aisha likewise identifying Iqra as first; Mujahid says it was followed by Nun and the pen.
rows.anchor: وقد أخرج الحاكم في المستدرك والبيهقي في الدلائل وصححاه عن عائشة نحوه

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: A report from Jabir calls Ya ayyuhal-Muddaththir the first revelation, but the earlier group offers several responses to it.
rows.anchor: وروي الشيخان عن أبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن قال سألت جابر بن عبد الله أي القرآن أنزل أولا

rows.speaker: أبو ميسرة عمرو بن شرحبيل
rows.claim: A trustworthy-transmitters but mursal report argues that al-Fatiha came first; the response is that it could refer to what followed Iqra and Muddaththir, and other reports are stronger.
rows.anchor: وقيل الفاتحة واحتج له بحديث مرسل رجاله ثقات أخرجه البيهقي في الدلائل

rows.speaker: جابر بن زيد
rows.claim: Jabir ibn Zayd gives the order Iqra, Nun, al-Muzzammil, al-Muddaththir, then al-Fatiha.
rows.anchor: وجزم جابر بن زيد بأن أول ما نزل اقرأ ثم ن ثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view holds that only the opening of Iqra through what he did not know was revealed first and the remainder came later, as suggested by Aisha's account of the first revelation.
rows.anchor: وقيل أول ما نزل صدرها إلى ما لم يعلم في غار حراء ثم نزل آخرها بعد ذلك

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha’s account says revelation paused soon after the opening verses; a report from Jabir then recounts how revelation resumed with al-Muddaththir.
rows.anchor: قالت ثم لم ينشب ورفة أن توفي وفتر الوحي

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir's account of Muddaththir explicitly concerns the period after revelation paused and then resumed, undermining its use as the first revelation overall.
rows.anchor: ويعلم منه ضعف الأستدلال على كون سورة المدثر أول نازل من القرآن على الإطلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi follows the view that the opening of Iqra was the first revelation outright, supported by Aisha's highly authentic report; ما أنا بقارئ is a statement of inability, not refusal, which would otherwise be grave disobedience.
rows.anchor: الصحيح كما قال البعض وهو الذي اختاره إن صدر هذه السورة الكريمة هو أول ما أنزل من القرآن

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf takes Jabir's claim to concern the first complete surah, while Sahih Muslim's commentary distinguishes Iqra as first overall from Muddaththir as first after the hiatus; the claim that al-Fatiha came first is plainly false.
rows.anchor: وفي الكشف الوجه حمل قول جابر على السورة الكاملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding surah described humanity's best form; this surah explains its material origin in clinging blood and expands on its afterlife condition, linking the two surahs thematically.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر سبحانه في سورة التين خلق الإنسان في أحسن تقويم بين عز وجل هنا أنه تعالى خلق الإنسان من علق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Read has an implied object, what is revealed of the Quran; the verb is not intransitive and باسم ربك is not its object with an extra ba, contrary to Abu Ubayda.
rows.anchor: إقرأ أي ما يوحى إليك من القرآن مقدر بقرينة المقام

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda treats the ba as extra and reads the command as Remember your Lord; al-Alusi rejects this, taking the ba as original accompaniment attached to read or an implied circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: بل هي أصلية ومعناها الملابسة وهي متعلقة بما عندها أو بمحذوف وقع حالا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: According to a reading attributed to Qatada, the command means begin or open with your Lord's name, saying the basmala and then reading; this supports requiring basmala when reading and has been used to argue it belongs to every surah, though al-Alusi notes debate.
rows.anchor: كما روي عن قتادة والمعنى اقرأ مبتدئا أو مفتتحا باسم ربك

rows.speaker: النووي
rows.claim: Some argue that the basmala is not Quran at the beginnings of surahs because it is absent from sound accounts of the first revelation; al-Nawawi reports this argument, while proponents answer that it descended later.
rows.anchor: وبعضهم استدل على أنها ليست بقرآن في أوائل السور بأنها لم تذكر فيما صح من أخبار بدء الوحي

rows.speaker: عكرمة، الحسن
rows.claim: Ikrima and Hasan say the basmala was the first Quranic revelation; al-Dahhak's report from Ibn Abbas says Gabriel first instructed Muhammad to seek refuge and say it. Al-Suyuti counts this as the first revelation, but al-Alusi objects that this does not follow.
rows.anchor: وهذا خلاف ما أخرج الواحدي عن عكرمة والحسن أنهما قالا أول ما نزل من القرآن بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi prefers the ba as accompaniment because that avoids implying God's name is an instrument; it may alternatively indicate seeking aid.
rows.anchor: وجوز كون الباء للأستعانة متعلقة بما عندها أو بمحذوف وقع حالا ورجحت الملابسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is not impossible even if immediate: the Prophet knows that whatever is revealed as Quran is what he must read, so the command itself can be part of the material to read.
rows.anchor: ثم أنه ليس في الأمر المذكور تكليف بما لا يطاق سواء دل الأمر على الفور أم لا

rows.speaker: الآمدي
rows.claim: Al-Amidi cites the repeated command Read followed by this passage as an example of clarification delayed until after the original command; al-Alusi accepts the passage as the clarification but rejects making the whole passage or basmala the object of the earlier command.
rows.anchor: قال الآمدي عند ذكر أدلة جواز تأخير البيان عن وقت الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God Lord and adding the possessive for Muhammad recalls divine nurturing and his gradual attainment of human perfection through recurring revelation.
rows.anchor: والتعرض لعنوان الربوبية المنبئة عن التربية والتبليغ إلى الكمال اللائق شيئا فشيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Who created recalls God's original favor and ability to teach reading; it may mean the one who creates or the one who created everything, and it rules out idols as true lords because Arabs did not ascribe creation to them.
rows.anchor: ووصف الرب بقوله تعالى الذي خلق لتذكيره عليه الصلاة والسلام أول النعماء الفائضة عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human is singled out as the noblest creation, whose remarkable design strongly demonstrates the worship implied by the reading command; repeating it may also magnify it by first leaving it indefinite.
rows.anchor: إنه أشرف المخلوقات وفيه من بدائع الصنع والتدبير ما فيه أدل على وجوب العبادة المقصودة من القراءة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says mentioning human creation after the command to read signals that humanity was created for Quranic reading and understanding, as in the opening of al-Rahman.
rows.anchor: وعن الزمخشري أن المناسب أن يراد خلق الإنسان بعد الأمر بقراءة القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clinging blood displays God's power through the sharp contrast between the human's initial and later states; the plural form matches humanity as a genus and preserves the rhyme.
rows.anchor: لبيان كمال قدرته تعالى بإظهار ما بين حالتيه الأولى والآخرة من التباين البين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation for naming this stage is that sperm and earth are farther from developed humanity, although they might seem even clearer proofs of divine power.
rows.anchor: ولعله على ما قيل السر في تخصيص هذا الطور من بين سائر أطواره

rows.speaker: البحر
rows.claim: Al-Bahr says the verse omits Adam's original material, earth, because disbelievers were not familiar with that creation; it instead mentions the derivative material to bring the point nearer to their understanding, though al-Alusi says this does not fully answer the question.
rows.anchor: وفي البحر لم يذكر سبحانه مادة الأصل يعني آدم عليه السلام وهو التراب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view sees a reminder of the clinging blood removed from Muhammad's chest before his mission, preparing him for revelation and linking this surah to al-Sharh, especially if that surah means literal chest-splitting.
rows.anchor: وقيل خص هذا الطور تذكيرا له عليه الصلاة والسلام لما وقع من شرح الصدر قبل النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that human here means Adam created from something that clings to the hand is unacceptable to al-Alusi.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من زعم أن المراد بالإنسان آدم عليه السلام وإن المعنى خلق آدم من طبق يعلق باليد وهو مما لا تعلق به يد القبول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated command reinforces the obligation and prepares the way for the next statement about God's generosity, removing the Prophet's excuse that reading belongs to literate people; the command is to read beginning in God's name.
rows.anchor: اقرأ أي افعل ما أمرت به تأكيدا للأيجاب وتمهيدا لما يعقبه من قوله تعالى وربك الأكرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God taught people through the pen and writing, and can teach the Prophet without that means; karam is giving what is fitting without ulterior motive, and in its absolute intensive form it is uniquely God's attribute.
rows.anchor: الذي علم بالقلم أي علم ما علم بواسطة القلم لا غيره تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative treats the second Read as not emphasis but as a lead-in to remove the Prophet's excuse, making Your Lord is most generous a circumstantial clause about the command's subject.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن لا يكون اقرأ هذا تأكيدا للأول وإنما ذكر ليوصل به ما يزيح العذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is an explanatory substitution for teaching by the pen: God teaches humans with and without writing all kinds of knowledge they had not imagined; the omitted first object and explicit lack of prior knowledge stress divine power and generosity and the Prophet's vast learning.
rows.anchor: بدل اشتمال من علم بالقلم أي علمه به وبدونه من الأمور الكلية والجزئية والجلية ما لم يخطر بباله

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Some supply script as the object of taught, supported by Ibn al-Zubayr's reading الذي علم الخط بالقلم.
rows.anchor: وقدر بعضهم مفعول علم الخط وجعل بالقلم متعلقا به وأيد بقراءة ابن الزبير الذي علم الخط بالقلم

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbai says the first Read commands personal reading or reading generally, while the second is reading for proclamation; another view connects the latter to prayer, and the Lord's generosity clause could be circumstantial or independent.
rows.anchor: ولجبائي أن اقرأ الأول أمر بالقراءة لنفسه وقيل مطلقا والثاني أمر بالقراءة للتبليغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the reading is for proclamation, the command means to tell one's people that the generous Lord rewards work, strengthens the Prophet to retain the Quran, and enables its delivery.
rows.anchor: وحاصل المعنى على إرادة القراءة للتبليغ في قول بلغ قومك وربك الأكرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says the clearest interpretation is that the second Read reinforces the first; the proposal to attach the basmala's باسم to the second command to make God's name the exclusive starting point is far-fetched because it normally attaches to the adjacent command.
rows.anchor: وأولى الأوجه وأظهرها التأكيد وأبعد بعضهم جدا فزعم أن بسم في البسملة متعلق باقرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fronted command suits the importance of reading in the first surah revealed; even if another passage preceded it, the sense is read beginning with God's name, so other openings would not comply, while moving the name first changes the focus.
rows.anchor: ولا يخفى أن الظاهر تعلق باسم ربك بما عنده وتقديم الفعل ههنا أوقع

rows.speaker: الضحاك، كعب
rows.claim: The verse does not identify the teacher; reports say every prophet who wrote, or name Idris and Adam as the first writers. Al-Alusi doubts claims that they invented particular alphabets.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو كل نبي كتب وقال الضحاك هو إدويس عليه السلام وهو أول من خط وقال كعب هو آدم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage praises writing’s benefits and high status: without it religion would not stand and life would not be sound; the pen and script alone suffice as a sign of God’s subtle wisdom.
rows.anchor: وقد أدمج سبحانه وتعالى التنبيه على فضل علم الكتابة لما فيه من المنافع العظيمة ونيل الرتب الفخيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing was ancient among non-Arab peoples but a later arrival among Arabs, especially in the Hijaz, according to the apparent historical reports.
rows.anchor: وظاهر الآثار أن الكتابة في الأمم غير العرب قديمة وفيهم حادثة لا سيما في أهل الحجاز

rows.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
rows.claim: The continuation of a pen poem uses an image of a jinn and eager hands around the writing tool to evoke the power of writing.
rows.anchor: وأرى الجني اشتارته أيد عواسل

rows.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another poem that al-Zamakhshari attributes to an unnamed poet praises calligraphic pens and the far reach of writing.
rows.anchor: ومما نسبه الزمخشري في ذلك لبعضهم وعنى على ما قيل نفسه ورواقم رقش كمثل أراقم

rows.speaker: الكلبي، الهيثم بن عدي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi and al-Haytham ibn Adi report that writing was ancient among non-Arabs but newly acquired in the Hijaz, transferred from Hira by Harb ibn Umayya after he learned it in the region of al-Anbar; the chain of reported teachers leads through Aslam ibn Sidra to Maramir ibn Murra.
rows.anchor: وأنهم أخذوا من أهل الأنبار وذكر الكلبي والهيثم بن عدي أن الناقل للخط العربي من العراق إلى الحجاز حرب ابن أمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Himyar reportedly used the separate, unjoined Musnad script, taught only with permission; one claim counts twelve major script families, which al-Alusi allows only if these are origins since derivative scripts are too many to count.
rows.anchor: وكان لها شأن عندهم فلا يتعاطاها إلا من إذن له تعلمها وأصناف الكتابة كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some scholars object to calling people most generous in correspondence, even though they regard it as modest praise for rulers, and criticize applying it to Jews or Christians; people should show reverence and gratitude for the generosity of their Lord.
rows.anchor: ولم ير بعض العلماء من الأدب وصف غيره تعالى كما يفعله كثير من الناس في رسائلهم
